(II)--a mind-born daughter of ब्रह्मा given to वज्राङ्ग, son of Diti and कश्यप; she performed penance with her husband when Indra disturbed her by assuming different fearful disguises. She represented this to her husband at the end of his penance, and was blessed with a son, तारक. When he vanquished Indra, she became pleased. M. १४६. ५८; Ch. १४७ (whole).

(I) (also वाराह)--an incarnation of Hari; born out of ब्रह्मा's nostrils; roaring, he entered the waters and rescued the earth above, after vanquishing the Asura who attacked him. Prayer to, by the sages.
1: भा. III. १३. १८-45; X. 2. ४०; Vi. V. 5. १५.
Slew Hira- ण्याक्ष in the Sumana hill of प्लक्षद्वीप.
2: Br. II. १९. १३; III. ३६. ११; ७२. ७३-8.
The third अवतार्।
3: M. ४७. ४३.

4: Ib. ४७. ४७.
mother-earth taken to रसातलम्, appealed to [page३-154+ ३४] विष्णु for protection; he took up the वराह अवतार् and released the earth above the waters by raising her with his teeth;
5: Ib. Chh. २४७ and २४८; १०२. ११.
his next अवतार् was वामन;
6: Ib. १२२. १६; २४४. 6.

(I)--(विष्णु). An अवतार् of Hari who raised the earth from the waters, see वराह, the form which विष्णु takes in the श्वेतकल्प with four feet, four hands, etc., becomes Samvatsara and assumes the form of यज्ञ; the four yugas are four feet, the क्रतुस् are अङ्गस् or limbs, the four Vedas are the hands ऋतु, सन्धिमुखस्, two अयनस् are the faces and eyes, three पर्वस् are the heads, etc.,
1: भा. XI. 4. १८; वा. २३. १०३-7; ४८. ४०; ४९. ११; Vi. I. 4. 8, २६.
appro- priate to water sports; description of;
2: Br. I. 5. ११, ff.
helped by माया, wife (छाया-वा। प्।) out of the recovered earth came mountains and seven worlds; creation of human beings;
3: Ib. I. 5. १९.
where ब्रह्मा is said to assume this form.
4: Ib. II. 7. 7-9.
(II)--a Mt. afraid of हिरण्यकशिपु's arms. M. १६३. ८१.
(III)--the २६थ् kalpa. M. २९०. 9.
(IV)--the present kalpa; fourteen Manus be- ginning with स्वायम्भुव; name and features explained. वा. २१. १२, २३, २६ f. Vi. I. 3. २८; II. 1. ४३.
--Here विष्णु as वराह worshipped शिव; bath on the १२थ् day of the dark or bright half of the month leads to विष्णुलोकम्. M. १९३. ७३-74.

--a प्रदेश in जम्बूद्वीप;
1: वा. ४८. १४.
of different म्लेच्छस्; here is वराह Mt. from which the R. वाराही flows; sacred to विष्णु who took the boar अवतार्।
2: Ib. ४८. ३६-40.
--sacred to जया. M. १३. ३२. [page३-155+ ४७]
--an Apsaras; brought forth eight children. वा. ६९. ४८.
--a son of Pulaha and गती. भा. IV. 1. ३८.
--a son of सावर्णि Manu. M. 9. ३३.

(I)--(see मीत्रावरुण) King of the Asuras; when called upon to fight by हिरण्यकशिपु, he said that his passion was in a subdued state, and asked him to meet Hari in battle;
1: भा. II. 1. ३२; 7. ३१; III. १७. २७-30.
Once वरुण is said to have conquered all the world and performed the राजसूय compared to Yudhi- ष्ठिर's. Presented पृथु with a white umbrella: noted for much wealth. Protected क्रौञ्चद्वीप. Bali was bound with his noose;
2: Ib. III. १७. २८; X. ७४. १३; IV. १५. १४; २२. ५९; V. २०. १९; २४. २३.
A son of Aditi: his wife was चर्षणी
3: Ib. VI. 6. ३९; १८. 4; M. 6. 4; १७१. ५६; वा. ६६. ६६; ८४. 6.
(सुनादेवी- वा। प्।) propitiated by हरिश्चन्द्र, वरुण gave him a son on condition that he offered him in a sacrifice to him. Though reminded a number of times, हरिश्चन्द्र evaded fulfilling his promise and consequently got the disease, महोदर। But his son Rohita purchased सुनश्शेप as his substitute. वरुण was pleased and relieved him of his disease.
4: भा. IX. 7. 8-२२.
Helped ऋचीक in securing a thousand white horses with black ears for his शुल्क।
5: Ib. IX. १५. 7.
ऋतुमत् in the त्रिकूट hill was his pleasure garden.
6: Ib. VIII. 2. 9.
Fought with हेती in the देवासुर war. In the तारकामय, when Indra lost his fortune, वरुण conferred with the gods and ब्रह्मा how to restore it.
7: Ib. VIII. 5. १७; १०. २८; ११. ४२; M. १५३. १७९-83; १५४. ४८७; १७४. १५; १७५. २२; १७७. ४९.
Offered sacrifice by वसिष्ठ on behalf of श्राद्ध deva; a लोकपाल. Description of the sacrifice.
8: भा. IX. 1. १३; १३. 6; १४. १७; III. 6. १३; Br. III. 1. १६; 3. ६७; M. २६६. २३.
When Nanda took bath once at आसुरीवेऌअ, an asura took him to वरुण. Welcomed कृष्ण, apologised for the capture of Nanda, and released him. Presented कृष्ण, horses for his new city. Got back his umbrella taken by Naraka, from कृष्ण who killed him;
9: भा. X. २८. 2-१०; ५०. ५६; ५९. २२ [2 and 3]; Vi. V. २९. १०, ३४; ३०. 1.
was sent against कृष्ण taking पारि- [page३-156+ ४२] जात from Indra's place but beaten by गरुड, went back; supplied बलराम at Vraja with वारुणी. His city सुखा on the west of Meru was visited by Arjuna who sojourned in search of the dead child of the द्वारका Bra1hmana.
११: भा. X. ८९. ४४; Br. II. २१. ३२.
Identified with Hari.
१२: भा. XI. १६. १७.
Lord of waters, an आदित्य, and a face of शिव.
१३: Br. II. २३. 5, १०३; २४. ३३ and ३७; २६. ४१. III. 7. २५४; २४. 4; ५७. ३५; M. 8. 3; ३१. १२; वा. ३४. ८९; १०८. ३१, ३३; Vi. I. १५. १३१; २२. 3.
Vanquished by रावण; finding him unwilling to give audience, परशुराम took up शिव's bow when वरुण appeared and begged to be excused; gave up गोकर्ण.
१४: Br. III. 8. 7; ५७. ३५-74; ५८. 8-३१.

१६: M. ६० 49; ६१. २८-31; २०१. २३-9.
Makara as his rid- ing animal; worship of in गृहबलि and before commence- ment of palace building; chariot of;

penance at बदरी; services of; in churning the ocean whence he received the umbrella;

a लोकपाल in the city of सुखा;

worshipped with अवभृताग्नि;

--of the four वर्णस्; could take to other professions in extreme cases. The आश्रम dharma; specific duties of the वानप्रस्थ and सन्न्यास.
1: भा. VII. ११. १४-24; XI. १७. १३-58; ch. १८ (whole) . वा. 8. १६८-75.

--a वैष्णवी vidya1, taught by विश्वरूप to Indra. Here the various manifestations of Hari [page३-162+ २५] including that of the Buddha are recalled. Once a certain कौशिकन् practised this and gave up his life in a desert. When a Gandharva crossed the bones of this dead man, he fell down on the earth. Instructed by वालखिल्यस्, he collected the bones, and after throwing them into the सरस्वती, and bathing there, returned to his place. Taught originally to त्वष्ट्रि by Dadhyanga; त्वष्ट्रि taught it to विश्वरूप. भा. VI. 8 (whole); 9. ५३.

--शिव addresses पार्वती on, in taking her out and showing the grandeur and majesty of the forest and garden round about काशी; the place of विद्या- [page३-198+ ४१] dharas, Siddhas and चारणस्. Here भगवान् Pin3gala became गणेश्वर and क्षेत्रपाल and distributor of food to the residents in the city. He was originally a यक्ष, son of पूर्णभद्र. He devoted himself to severe austerities and was blessed by शिव to be a गणपति.
1: M. ch. १८०.
It is अविमुक्त तीर्थ for here शिव is omnipresent and is never absent from there. All sinners who die here become Rudras in time. शिव stands here like a pillar, motionless till the deluge. Every part of the city is holy.
2: Ib. ch. १८१.
He who remains here for a month gets the benefit of observ- ing the पाशुपत vow. By living permanently one gets true emancipation. By giving up life at the मणिकर्णिका ghat one secures the desired goal. Perpetual life in काशी leads one to union with शिव.
3: Ib. ch. १८२.
काशी's importance on account of its sacred stream, the Ganges; survives all deluge; शिव addresses पार्- वती on the great glory of the क्षेत्रम् in terms of Parama- yoga, Paramagati and परममोक्ष. It is a place where people of all वर्णस् attain immortality. Gifts of cow and other things in this city are always beneficial.
4: Ib. ch. १८३.
It is the place where शिव got rid of the curse of ब्रह्मा to roam about with a skull for having cut off the fifth head of the creator. Through the grace of Hari, the skull fell down in काशी and broke into a thousand pieces.
5: Ib. ch. १८४.
It is the burial ground of all the gods, the ground being the Avimukta temple. It is the seat of ब्रह्मा. But it deludes non- devotees. Here वेदव्यास resided for १२ years observing the vow of silence. At the end of the vow he felt hungry and asked for alms. None was able to feed him. When he was about to curse the city, शिव and पार्वती took the human form and entertained him to his satisfaction. Then व्यास knew of his guests who remarked that a man of choleric temper like himself should not live in that city. But he was permitted to visit it twice a fortnight on अष्टमि and चतुर्दशी days.
